commit.message:
fix[tool]: raise user errors for malformed input files (#5080)

Storage layout override files and imported JSON ABI files are user
input, but several malformed files crashed through internal-error paths:
bad layout overrides could raise CompilerPanic, TypeError or KeyError,
and invalid JSON ABI stateMutability values reached StringEnum._missing_
and raised CompilerPanic.

Validate storage-layout traversal and slot values before reserving
slots, downgrade reachable layout roundtrip mismatches to
StorageLayoutException, and validate JSON ABI stateMutability before
constructing the internal enum.

Valid files still compile, and malformed files are still rejected. The
change is that user input errors now produce typed user-facing
exceptions instead of internal compiler errors.

commit.message:
fix[venom]: register self in global analyses cache fallback (#5084)

Fallback global-analysis initialization can create a function cache
separate from the one used by the active pass. Invalidation then leaves
global consumers reading stale local analysis results.

Give each function a stable canonical cache within the global registry.
Bind local consumers once per registry and delegate requests,
invalidations and forced refreshes to the canonical cache. Rebind when
compiler phases replace the registry and register newly added functions
before fresh global analyses.

Use isolated caches in validators so stale pass results cannot hide
malformed IR after a missed invalidation.

---------

Co-authored-by: Harry Kalogirou <harry@kalogirou.net>
Co-authored-by: Harry Kalogirou <harkal@nlogn.eu>

commit.message:
fix[codegen]: fix `convert()` codegen in venom pipeline (#4979)

the venom pipeline `convert()` had several mismatches with the legacy
pipeline:

- decimal bounds checking used integer division for pre-multiplication
  clamping, which truncated towards negative infinity instead of towards
  zero. for negative inputs close to `DECIMAL_MIN / DECIMAL_DIVISOR`,
  this could produce a pre-lo bound that was one unit too high, allowing
  out-of-range values to pass the clamp and wrap around after scaling.

- `_check_literal_int_bounds` only handled plain int/bool constants. hex
  literals (`0xff`), bytes constants, and bytestring constants were
  silently skipped, so `convert(0xffff, uint8)` compiled without error
  instead of raising InvalidLiteral. additionally, sign extension was
  missing for hex/bytes-to-signed-integer conversions (e.g.
  `convert(0xff <bytes1>, int16)` should yield -1, not 255).

- there was no `_check_literal_decimal_bounds` at all, so compile-time
  overflow checks for decimal conversions (e.g. converting a too-large
  int136 to decimal) were absent in the venom pipeline.

refactor `_get_folded_value` to return the AST node instead of the
python value, so literal-kind information (hex vs decimal vs bytes) is
available for legacy-compatible sign-extension and bounds checks. add
sign extension for hex/bytes constants converted to signed types. add a
separate `_check_literal_decimal_bounds` with correct round-towards-zero
division. use `arg_node.reduced()` to resolve constant variable
references before type-checking bytestring inputs.

parent bb7ee4955b65b3e7ab45f21562e8f03b3e6ac493

commit.message:
refactor[lang]: simplify typing logic around inf (#5233)

before d3c150e, the codegen type of an expression was always the
expected type. with d3c150e this no longer works, as the expected type
can now contain wildcard lengths, which are not encodable (need to be
resolved to a finite length or `INF`). to solve this issue, it added
`_annotation_type` which derives an encodable type from the inferred and
expected type.

this commit refactors `_annotation_type` to give it nice properties, and
to validate its invariants:

`_interpolate` finds the smallest type between its two parameters, which
contains no wildcards. this allows us to remove
`empty_list_candidate_types` which represented a kind of regression of
3867629 (and thus re-introduced similar issues).

to support the above/fix bugs it uncovered, a couple more minor things
are done:
* fix (codegen's) `Expr.parse_IfExp`'s not copying `~empty` into memory.
* fix `_ExprAnalyser.types_from_Subscript` producing multitypes
  containing the same type twice.
* fix not being able to do `my_type.has_wildcard` because
  `_GenericTypeAcceptor` didn't have it.
* let mypy know that `SArrayT.length` is always an int.

commit.message:
fix[lang]: forbid assignment to values (#5181)

the left hand-side of assignments used to only be checked to have
correct mutability and location. however some expressions fulfilled
these criterion without representing a concrete offset in
memory/transient/storage, for example 'self.g()[0] = 5'. this commit
addresses that by directly checking that the lhs has a location.

commit.message:
fix[venom]: round int to decimal clamp bound toward zero (#5298)

The lower pre-scale bound in _to_decimal used floor division, so
for negative bounds it was one below the legacy bound and venom
accepted one input that legacy rejects, producing a decimal below
MIN_DECIMAL. Use truncating division, matching legacy.

commit.message:
chore[docs]: document `block.prevhash` at block 0 (#5291)

`block.prevhash` compiles to a bare `blockhash(number - 1)`, without the
clamps that the `blockhash()` builtin adds and without the underflow
check that `block.number - 1` gets in user code. at block 0,
`blockhash(block.number - 1)` reverts, while `block.prevhash` evaluates
to zero.

the compiler assumes the block number is never 0 on real chains, so
instead of adding the checks (and their gas cost) to `block.prevhash`,
document the difference next to the other notes on environment
variables.

fixes GH 5146

commit.message:
fix[venom]: fix concat buffer overrun with bytesM args (#5295)

bytesM args are stored with full-word mstores at unaligned offsets, so
a store near the end of the data can write up to 31 bytes past the
concat output buffer. size the buffer to cover the furthest byte any
bytesM store can reach.

commit.message:
fix[venom]: match legacy for appends to removed rows (#5281)

match legacy's rejection of an append whose argument removes the row
being appended to. venom previously checked the row too early and then
silently wrote into it after removal.

recheck the array positions after evaluating the argument. reuse the
original positions to keep venom's evaluation order and avoid running
index expressions twice.
